subject: Order form/MSA: notice windows, auto-renew options, and termination-for-convenience carveouts
messages:
From: procurement@acme.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify auto-renew and termination for convenience (MSA + Order Form)

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Our legal/procurement team has a few outstanding items on the MSA and the attached Order Form. Two quick asks we hope you can help with before we go back to execs:

1) Auto-renew: your MSA currently has a 30-day opt-out window prior to renewal. We are trying to standardize to a 60-day notice to align with our procurement cycle. Can Redwood confirm flexibility here and whether an initial pilot term could have a shorter notice?

2) Termination for convenience: we need to understand if Redwood will accept a limited termination-for-convenience right and whether there are transition obligations (data export, retention of logs, assist for 30 days). Also curious if any financial consequences (prorated refunds, early-termination fees) would apply.

Attaching our redlines (Acme_Redlines_MSA_v2.docx) and a marked-up order form.

Would appreciate a coordinated response from Redwood legal + AE.

Best,
Alice Patel
Sourcing Manager, Acme Corporation
procurement@acme.com

Attachment: Acme_Redlines_MSA_v2.docx (docx)
Attachment: OrderForm-Acme-20270415.pdf (pdf)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Alice Patel <alice.patel@acme.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify auto-renew and termination for convenience (MSA + Order Form)

Alice — thanks for the clear summary and the redlines. Looping in Laura (legal) and Aditya (your AE) so we can provide a single set of proposed language.

Quick read: we can be flexible on the notice window depending on term length. Two options we can propose back to you:
- Standard annual term: 60-day opt-out window prior to auto-renewal (matches your ask).
- Pilot / initial 3-6 month term: 30-day opt-out (to allow a shorter onboarding pilot cadence).

On termination for convenience, Redwood prefers a limited approach that preserves predictability for capacity planning. Typical approach we use:
- Mutual termination-for-convenience allowed after the initial commitment period (eg, after first 6 months).
- 30-day transition assistance (data export + reasonable cooperation) without additional fees; any prepaid, unused committed fees would be prorated and refunded.

Laura — could you propose precise MSA wording and flag any commercial caveats? I attached a quick annotated MSA draft (Redwood_MSA_annotated_v3.docx) with the two notice options and the limited TFC language.

Next step: Laura to provide markups, then we can do a 30-minute call with Acme legal to finalize. Does early next week work for you, Alice?

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
Mobile: (415) 555-0198

Attachment: Redwood_MSA_annotated_v3.docx (docx)

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, Alice Patel <alice.patel@acme.com>
Date: Sat, 17 Apr 2027 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify auto-renew and termination for convenience (MSA + Order Form)

Karthik / team — drafting notes below (high level) and then I'll add redline comments in the attached file. Sending early so Acme has visibility.

1) Auto-renew / notice window
- Accept 60-day notice for standard annual terms. For pilots (<= 6 months) we can accept 30 days. We should capture this as a single sentence in Section 2.1: "Unless otherwise agreed in the Order Form, the initial Term is [..]; thereafter the Agreement renews for successive terms equal to the initial Term unless either party provides written notice of non-renewal at least [60/30] days prior to the end of the then-current Term (60 days for terms >=12 months; 30 days for Pilot Terms <=6 months)".

Rationale: gives Sales flexibility while keeping clarity for procurement.

2) Termination for Convenience (TFC)
- Recommend limited mutual TFC after the Initial Commitment Period (e.g., 6 months). Before that, TFC should be disallowed.
- If we accept TFC, require: (i) 30 days' prior written notice; (ii) Redwood provides 30 days of transition assistance (scope: export of customer data and reasonable technical assistance); (iii) proration for prepaid fees and refund of unused committed capacity where applicable.
- Exclude any TFC carve for cases where Dedicated Reserved Capacity is committed and already provisioned with hardware/slots that cannot be reallocated without commercial impact; in those cases, propose an early-termination fee equal to remaining committed minimums for the then-current quarter.

3) Order Form: include explicit checkbox in the OF that toggles Pilot vs Standard Term to make the notice logic machine-checkable. This simplifies procurement workflows.

4) Canary / fallback: propose adding a short "service degradation / transition" clause that allows for limited staggered termination windows if the customer requests partial offboarding by region. This is optional but requested by some enterprise customers.

I'll add tracked changes and highlight any items where Commercial needs to sign off (eg, early-termination fees for Dedicated).

Suggested next steps:
- I will upload a redline to the shared draft by EOD Sunday.
- Karthik / Aditya: please confirm if you're okay with the Dedicated carve and whether we should treat it as negotiable.
- Alice: can we schedule a 30-minute legal sync on Mon or Tue? Please propose two slots.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Compliance
Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai

Attachment: Redwood_MSA_annotated_v3.docx (docx)

Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify auto-renew and termination for convenience (MSA + Order Form)

Thanks, Laura and team. That approach sounds reasonable. A few quick notes from Acme side:

- We can accept the 60/30 split you propose so long as the Order Form clearly marks a Term as "Pilot" or "Standard". Procurement automation needs that field.
- On TFC: we prefer mutual TFC after 3 months for pilots and 6 months for standard, but are willing to accept 6 months across the board if Redwood needs predictability. We do want the 30-day transition assistance and the data export guarantee spelled out.
- Regarding Dedicated capacity: we believe any early-termination fee should be proportional and capped; happy to review a simple schedule (eg, prorated remaining committed months capped at 3 months of committed fees).

Let's take Laura up on a quick call Monday morning PT — available 10:30–11:00 or 16:00–16:30 PT. Which works for you?

Appreciate the responsiveness.

Best,
Alice
Sourcing Manager, Acme Corporation
